scope.timing: Stage wall time includes commands and in-stage filesystem work. Validation, statfs, and temporary-directory cleanup are outside stage timings. The independently measured nativeConventional arm does not export private data or perform restore and second drop. The native arm includes private export and recovery for a stronger-semantics comparison with Graft; do not label it ordinary Git performance. Primary setup starts after initialization and includes creating and packing history, the checkout, and the initial offline install. Any history duplication in a workspace is charged where it occurs.
scope.disk: Signed volume-wide statfs bfree * bsize, relative to the populated primary with its own packed history and warm npm cache. Tracked changes and private files are added after seed because shared seed requires a clean index and tracked checkout. Background writes and delayed allocation can affect samples. The gc checkpoint includes retained recovery bytes. The logical comparison sums regular-file lengths within the fixture root, including every CoW copy at its apparent size.
scope.apfsFileData: Union of APFS allocation blocks mapped to regular-file data within EOF, by device, within each arm root. Shared blocks and hardlinks count once. Directory and inode metadata, xattrs and resource forks are outside scope. A failed mapping invalidates all extent deltas for that arm. Observer time is excluded and reported separately. Scans can warm filesystem metadata caches, so omit --apfs-file-data for timing-only runs.
scope.recovery: The native fixture retains a dropped commit in a separate bare repository and moves known private files before removal. Its restore fetches and checks out that commit and returns the saved dependency tree and scratch file. Native retains the landed build and dependency files and uses integration to retain the landed commit. These steps cover this fixture. Graft uses its public recovery and may retain more state, including the full retired private repository.
scope.resources: Optional per-command /usr/bin/time CPU and maximum RSS, with OS-specific child accounting. Stage and run CPU sum their command samples; peak RSS is their maximum, not simultaneous process-tree memory. Node harness filesystem work and validation are outside resource accounting. Executable sizes exclude shared libraries.

nativeRecoveryComparison.scope: Independent native runs with and without private retention, restore and second drop. The paired difference includes normal run-to-run noise; preparation time and recovery stages are also reported separately.
